messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Construct a configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the largest minimum triangle area you can; the score is the smallest area among all 286 triangles formed by triples of your 13 points, every point must lie in [0,1]x[0,1] and all 13 points must be distinct.

Stay within this direction: number-theoretic lattice cosets with provable minimum-determinant bounds via Minkowski

Generate 10 candidate conjectures within that direction, sampled from the
full distribution of responses you could give. For each, give the
conjecture and your estimated probability that it is the response you would
give to this prompt. Every candidate's probability must be below 0.10.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"candidates": [{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>", "probability": <number below 0.10>}, ... 10 items]}

message.content: {"candidates": [{"conjecture": "Place points at the 13 elements of Z[ω]/(13) projected onto the fundamental parallelogram of Q(√-3), scaled to fit [0,1]². The minimum triangle area equals 1/(6·13²) ≈ 0.000197, proved via Minkowski's theorem on the sublattice of index 13² in the hexagonal lattice, which bounds the minimal determinant from below by the covolume ratio.", "probability": 0.09}, {"conjecture": "Select 13 points from the coset (1/13)Z² ∩ [0,1]² with coordinates {(i, i² mod 13)/13 : i=0,...,12}. The minimum triangle area is 1/13², with the bound proved by showing any three points form a sublattice coset whose Minkowski lower bound on the determinant exceeds 1/13².", "probability": 0.08}, {"conjecture": "Take the 13 points of the regular 13-gon inscribed in the unit square's incircle, translated to center at (0.5,0.5). The minimum area is sin(2π/13)/4 ≈ 0.1164, with optimality proved via Minkowski's convex body theorem applied to the cyclotomic lattice Z[ζ₁₃] restricted to the real embedding.", "probability": 0.07}, {"conjecture": "Use the 13-point configuration from the projective plane PG(2,3) embedded via a quadratic number field into [0,1]². The minimum triangle area is 1/156, proved by Minkowski's theorem on the associated trace form lattice, which gives a provable lower bound of 1/(12·13) on all 3×3 minors.", "probability": 0.06}, {"conjecture": "Construct 13 points as a scaled translate of the shortest-vector coset of the Leech lattice mod 13, projected to 2D. The minimum triangle area is 1/169, with Minkowski's second theorem providing the determinant bound via the product formula for successive minima in the 2D projection.", "probability": 0.05}, {"conjecture": "Place 13 points at the intersections of the unit square with a rotated copy of (1/√13)Z² at angle arctan(1/3). The minimum triangle area is 1/(4·13) ≈ 0.0192, with the class number 1 property ensuring all 3-point sublattices meet the determinant lower bound.", "probability": 0.04}, {"conjecture": "Take the 13 points of a Costas array permutation of order 13, scaled to [0,1]² by dividing by 12. The minimum triangle area is 1/144, proved via Minkowski's theorem on the associated Welch-bound-saturating difference set lattice.", "probability": 0.04}, {"conjecture": "Place 13 points at (i/12, {i·α}/1) for i=0,...,12 where α = (1+√5)/2 is the golden ratio and {·} is the fractional part.
